modules.sourceReference: Day 1 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 7; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 1 recap
modules.title: Day 1 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the difference between a project and an operation?
questions.explanation: A project is temporary and creates a unique result; operations are ongoing and repetitive.

options.label: A project is temporary and unique; operations are ongoing and repetitive
A project is ongoing; operations always have a fixed end date
Projects produce reports; operations produce physical products
There is no meaningful difference

questions.question: Name the five phases of the project lifecycle.
questions.explanation: The lifecycle phases are Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Control, and Closure.

options.label: Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Control, Closure
Discovery, Design, Coding, Testing, Support
Scope, Time, Cost, Quality, Risk
Request, Approval, Purchase, Delivery, Payment

questions.question: What is the triple constraint?
questions.explanation: The triple constraint balances project scope, time and cost.

options.label: Scope, time and cost
People, process and technology
Risk, quality and communication
Initiation, execution and closure

questions.question: What are the five process groups?
questions.explanation: The process groups are Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring & Controlling, and Closing.

options.label: Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring & Controlling, Closing
Concept, Design, Build, Launch, Maintain
Scope, Schedule, Budget, Quality, People
Request, Review, Approve, Deliver, Audit

questions.question: What are the core responsibilities of a project manager?
questions.explanation: The project manager plans, leads, communicates, monitors, controls and closes the project.

options.label: Plan, lead, communicate, monitor, control and close
Write all code and perform every project task
Approve only the budget and leave delivery to others
Avoid stakeholder communication until closure

modules.sourceReference: Day 2 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 13; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 2 recap
modules.title: Day 2 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is a project charter?
questions.explanation: A project charter formally authorises the project and establishes its purpose, objectives, high-level scope and key stakeholders.

options.label: The document that formally authorises a project
The detailed list of every project task and resource
The final report produced after project closure
A contract used only for external suppliers

questions.question: How do you prioritize stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Stakeholders are commonly prioritised by their level of power or influence and their interest in the project.

options.label: Assess their power or influence and their level of interest
Rank them only by job title
Engage only stakeholders who support the project
Prioritise them by the order in which they were identified

questions.question: What is a WBS?
questions.explanation: A Work Breakdown Structure decomposes project scope into smaller, manageable work packages.

options.label: A hierarchical decomposition of project work into manageable packages
A chart ranking stakeholder power and interest
A calculation of project cost variance
A register of completed lessons learned

questions.question: What is the critical path?
questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities and determines the shortest possible project duration.

options.label: The longest dependent sequence that determines project duration
The least expensive sequence of activities
The list of tasks assigned to the project manager
Every activity with an identified risk

questions.question: Name three cost estimation techniques.
questions.explanation: The module covers analogous, parametric and bottom-up cost estimation.

options.label: Analogous, parametric and bottom-up
Agile, Waterfall and Hybrid
Avoid, transfer and accept
Forming, storming and norming

modules.sourceReference: Day 3 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 18; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 3 guidance
modules.title: Day 3 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What are the four leadership styles?
questions.explanation: Situational leadership uses Directing, Coaching, Supporting and Delegating styles based on team needs.

options.label: Directing, Coaching, Supporting and Delegating
Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Closing
Avoiding, Transferring, Mitigating and Accepting
Formal, Informal, Written and Verbal

questions.question: Name Tuckman's five stages of team development.
questions.explanation: The stages are Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing and Adjourning.

options.label: Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing and Adjourning
Initiating, Planning, Executing, Controlling and Closing
Discovering, Designing, Building, Testing and Releasing
Directing, Coaching, Supporting, Delegating and Reviewing

questions.question: What are the five conflict resolution approaches?
questions.explanation: The module identifies Collaborate, Compromise, Accommodate, Avoid and Compete.

options.label: Collaborate, Compromise, Accommodate, Avoid and Compete
Plan, Assure, Control, Inspect and Close
Identify, Analyse, Transfer, Monitor and Audit
Direct, Coach, Support, Delegate and Escalate

questions.question: What makes an effective status report?
questions.explanation: A useful status report clearly shows overall status, accomplishments, planned work, and issues or risks.

options.label: Clear overall status, accomplishments, planned activities, and issues or risks
A complete transcript of every project conversation
Only positive news with no risks or issues
Technical details without an overall status

questions.question: What is the difference between quality assurance and quality control?
questions.explanation: Quality assurance is process-focused and prevents defects; quality control inspects deliverables and identifies defects.

options.label: Assurance improves processes; control inspects deliverables
Assurance happens after closure; control happens before initiation
Assurance manages cost; control manages schedule
They are the same activity

modules.sourceReference: Day 4 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 24; answers cross-checked with facilitator monitoring and risk guidance
modules.title: Day 4 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is EVM?
questions.explanation: Earned Value Management integrates scope, schedule and cost information to measure project performance.

options.label: A method integrating scope, schedule and cost to measure performance
A technique used only to identify stakeholders
A process for choosing a project methodology
A quality inspection performed at closure

questions.question: What does SPI < 1 mean?
questions.explanation: A Schedule Performance Index below 1 means the project is behind schedule.

options.label: The project is behind schedule
The project is ahead of schedule
The project is under budget
The project has no schedule variance

questions.question: What is the change control board?
questions.explanation: The change control board is the authorised group that reviews, approves, rejects or defers project change requests.

options.label: The group authorised to review and decide on change requests
The team that performs all project work
The supplier panel that sets contract prices
The group that writes the lessons learned report

questions.question: What are the risk response strategies?
questions.explanation: For threats, the module covers Avoid, Mitigate, Transfer and Accept.

options.label: Avoid, mitigate, transfer and accept
Initiate, plan, execute and close
Direct, coach, support and delegate
Measure, analyse, design and verify

questions.question: What's the difference between an issue and a risk?
questions.explanation: A risk is an uncertain future event; an issue has already occurred and requires action.

options.label: A risk may happen; an issue has already happened
A risk is always negative; an issue is always positive
A risk affects schedule; an issue affects only cost
There is no difference

modules.sourceReference: Day 5 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 30; answers cross-checked with facilitator closure and certification guidance
modules.title: Day 5 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What are the key closure activities?
questions.explanation: Closure includes obtaining acceptance, completing handover, closing contracts, releasing resources, archiving records and documenting lessons learned.

options.label: Acceptance, handover, contract closure, resource release, archiving and lessons learned
Creating the charter and identifying initial stakeholders
Estimating costs and building the first schedule
Avoiding documentation so the team can move quickly

questions.question: What is lessons learned?
questions.explanation: Lessons learned capture what worked, what did not and recommendations that can improve future projects.

options.label: Knowledge captured from project experience for use on future projects
A list of tasks that remain incomplete at closure
The final project budget approval
A replacement for stakeholder acceptance

questions.question: When would you choose Waterfall vs Agile?
questions.explanation: Waterfall suits stable, well-defined requirements; Agile suits evolving requirements and frequent feedback. Hybrid combines elements of both.

options.label: Waterfall for stable requirements; Agile for evolving requirements and frequent feedback
Waterfall for every software project; Agile only for construction
Agile when no stakeholder feedback is available
Choose solely according to project budget

questions.question: What are the PMP exam domains?
questions.explanation: The course identifies People, Process and Business Environment as the PMP exam domains.

options.label: People, Process and Business Environment
Scope, Time and Cost
Initiation, Planning and Closure
Waterfall, Agile and Hybrid

questions.question: What are the 10 knowledge areas?
questions.explanation: The ten are Integration, Scope, Schedule, Cost, Quality, Resource, Communications, Risk, Procurement and Stakeholder Management.

options.label: Integration, Scope, Schedule, Cost, Quality, Resource, Communications, Risk, Procurement and Stakeholder
Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Closing only
People, Process, Technology, Finance and Operations only
Waterfall, Agile, Scrum, Kanban and Hybrid only
